steps.title: Sangiovese
steps.body: Sangiovese is Tuscany's grape: sour cherry, herbs and earth, high acidity and firm, tea-like tannin. It has local names and clones: Brunello in Montalcino, Prugnolo Gentile in Montepulciano, Morellino in Scansano. Native partners include Canaiolo, Colorino and Mammolo.

steps.title: International grapes and whites
steps.body: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Syrah arrived in the 20th century, especially on the coast in Bolgheri. They're used in Super Tuscans and allowed in small amounts in Chianti Classico. White grapes include Vernaccia di San Gimignano, Tuscany's oldest DOCG white, Vermentino on the coast, and Trebbiano and Malvasia for Vin Santo.

steps.prompt: Match each name to its place.

steps.body: Vin Santo, Tuscany's sweet wine from dried Trebbiano and Malvasia, is served with cantucci almond biscuits.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sangiovese leads, with local names like Brunello
Bordeaux grapes thrive on the coast
Vernaccia, Vermentino and Vin Santo complete the whites
